categories.summary: No new confirmed attacks today. Iran still says Hormuz stays closed until the US lifts its blockade, and only about 2 ships a day get through. Taiwan, Korea and Russia-NATO show no new warning signs; a Latvian mobilisation drill this weekend is a planned exercise.

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal. Forecast markets put a Russian nuclear test this year at about 4%, still low.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure

sources.title: BleepingComputer: France blames Iranian hackers for supermarket attacks
Nextgov: US agencies warn of refrigeration hacks
Cyber Daily: attackers targeting US water systems could happen here

categories.summary: Hackers suspected of working for Iran have hit small US water stations, two tankers, and supermarket freezers in Europe, and are now probing newly found flaws in Copeland refrigeration controllers. France has blamed Iran; the US has warned but not formally blamed it. Apple had a major worldwide outage and says it was not an attack; US officials say there is no evidence the week's outages were attacks. Norway's Equinor reported a cyber attack on office systems with no effect on operations (not linked to Iran so far). Nothing reported in Australia; our banks, phones and grid are normal.

categories.name: Pandemic & biological

sources.title: WHO: Ebola (Bundibugyo) - DRC, Kenya and Nigeria

categories.summary: WHO reports Ebola continuing in parts of Africa, MERS in Qatar and Saudi Arabia, and a pneumonia of unknown cause in Russia; none is spreading toward Australia. Adelaide emergency departments are not unusually busy.

categories.name: Natural hazards

sources.title: Bureau of Meteorology: SA fire danger ratings

categories.summary: Fire danger in the Mount Lofty Ranges is Moderate today and High tomorrow, with gusts of 50-56 km/h Thursday and Friday. The Bureau has an Extreme fire weather warning for Yorke Peninsula tomorrow and storms in the far west. No fire bans or CFS warnings near home; recent fires in northern Adelaide were house and grass fires with no warnings.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: The VIX fear gauge rose about 11% to near 25.5, jumpy but not alarming. The Australian dollar slipped to about 67.2 US cents, making fuel dearer. Gold fell about 2%.

drivers: Suspected Iranian hackers are hitting water, tanker and supermarket-freezer systems in the US and Europe, and are now probing flaws in Copeland refrigeration controllers. If deliberate, the aim is to hit back over the Gulf war by disrupting allies' everyday services; next targets could include cold storage and water in countries like Australia, ports, and bank websites. This is a hypothesis: only France has formally blamed Iran.
A run of big outages overseas this week (US flights, Microsoft, Chase, Apple) were faults, not proven hacks; Coles is still investigating a real cyber incident here.

headline: Fire danger in the Hills rises to High tomorrow with gusty winds Thursday and Friday, a good evening to check your fire plan.
summary: Nothing new in the Gulf today: Iran still keeps Hormuz shut over the US blockade, so fuel stays dear. Apple had a big worldwide service outage and says it was not a cyber attack; together with the US flight halt, Microsoft and US bank outages, it is a run of big faults overseas, not proven attacks. Hackers suspected of working for Iran are still probing supermarket refrigeration controllers overseas, but nothing has hit Australia. Locally, fire danger in the Hills goes to High tomorrow, with an Extreme fire weather warning for Yorke Peninsula; there are no fire bans or CFS warnings near home.
